pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGE: api-gateway-edge-high-5xx — elevated 502/504s observed from edge -> gateway fanout. region=us-west-2, since=1709998960, p95 latency spiked. Pager: @sam (oncall)
sam (oncall): seeing it. jumps in. any quick signal on source?
maya (sre): checking proxies & upstream pools. initial spikes show >40% of requests hitting mux-proxy with 502s, connection reset from upstream cluster 'model-ingest'.
derek (edge): confirm: envoy clusters show 5xxs >= 70rps across 4 hosts. upstream health briefly flapping. maybe a TLS reneg - saw handshake timeouts. logs:```envoy error: connection failure, no healthy upstream: model-ingest-cluster```
jordan (product): are customers impacted? support dashboards show error rates on streaming endpoints up ~18%. Kristin filed a few incoming tickets.
kristin (support): yes two customers reported failed response (timeouts) for generation API. I posted a note to status.internal with initial impact.
sam (oncall): ok prioritize mitigation. maya, can we reduce fanout / circuit-break at gateway?
maya (sre): starting conservative mitigations: temporarily set cluster max_requests to 50 and enable fast-fail for model-ingest. running command:```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: envoy-config-patch-170999
data:
  envoy.yaml: |
    clusters:
      - name: model-ingest
        circuit_breakers:
          thresholds:
            - max_requests: 50
EOF```
apply in progress.
sam (oncall): deploy patch and watch. will also flip routing to secondary pool if it doesn't stabilize in 5 min.
derek (edge): spun up extra small pool in eu-west as warm fallback: routemgr failover start --cluster model-ingest --target eu-west-1 --health-check 30s
pagerbot: incidentbot: runbook 'gateway-5xx-spike' checklists enabled.
jordan (product): can we rate-limit heavy streaming clients? maybe an abusive prefix causing KV cache churn.
maya (sre): interesting — telemetry shows a single client_id making many long-lived chunked requests, holding KV cache entries and causing memory pressure on inferencer hosts. candidate cause.
kristin (support): flagged those customer IDs to CS. Should we throttle them server-side?
sam (oncall): yes, apply temporary soft-limit to that client:```iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.6 -j DROP``` (joke) — actually will apply per-client token bucket via gateway: set rate_limit for client_id=acme_streamer to 5r/s.
maya (sre): rate limit applied. also rolled out envoy config with circuit breakers. Early signal: tcp resets falling, 502 rate decreased to ~30% of prior. p95 latency improving.
derek (edge): failover to eu-west started; small portion of traffic (~10%) shifted. no errors on fallback.
sam (oncall): good. keep monitoring. @pagerbot please keep tracking and post hourly update. 
pagerbot: ack — next automated update in 10m.
10m later
pagerbot: automated update: 5xx rate down 78% from peak, p95 latency down 41%, incidents flagged: 8 customer errors still open.
jordan (product): Customer impact summary for SOC: PROD-impacted endpoints: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream. Estimated affected requests: 2.1k over 10m window. Severity: degraded (errors + timeouts).
kristin (support): pushing proactive emails to top 5 affected accounts. drafting status note.
maya (sre): follow-up root cause: a client upgrade rolled out a change that increased parallel chunked connections and disabled keepalive, causing frequent TLS handshakes and upstream worker exhaustion. mitigation steps: 1) rate-limit offending client 2) circuit-breaker at gateway 3) failover to secondary pool 4) temporary autoscale up for model-ingest hosts.
sam (oncall): plan to keep circuit-break active for 2-4 hours while we let infra scale and reach out to the client to request fix. Also schedule a canary test to validate keepalive behavior.
derek (edge): ops note: adjusted health check interval to 15s for model-ingest to avoid noisy flapping. updated runbook.
jordan (product): action items for postmortem: - coordinate with client on change - add a throttling policy for long-lived chunked streams - improve telemetry to surface per-client KV pressure - document rollback and playbook timings.
kristin (support): status.internal updated, external status page draft ready pending legal review.
sam (oncall): handing off to maya for overnight monitoring. Maya, you're primary until 1709999650. I'll remain available.
maya (sre): ack taking over. will monitor dashboards and escalate if >10% baseline 5xx resurfaces.
pagerbot: handoff note: oncall_transfer from sam to maya at 1709999400.
Final notes: small number of customers still seeing sporadic errors; mitigation successful for majority. postmortem scheduled in #postmortems at 1709999900. Attach logs: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1709999000/gateway-502-dump.log
:sheep: reactions: :thumbsup: from jordan, :eyes: from kristin, :white_check_mark: from derek
